findings.detail: Case-insensitive grep for ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, Kyber, Dilithium, SPHINCS, mlkem, mldsa, slhdsa over src/ + include/ returns 0 file hits. No post-quantum algorithm exists anywhere in the pinned tree; every signature is Ed25519 or secp256k1 ECDSA and every hash is SHA-512-Half.
findings.title: No post-quantum algorithm is present anywhere in the tree

findings.detail: Four methods create signatures with a server-held secret key: sign, sign_for, the signing path of submit, and channel_authorize (TransactionSign.cpp:676-682, PayChanClaim.cpp:92). Two more verify supplied signatures only: channel_verify and submit_multisigned (PayChanClaim.cpp:160, STTx.cpp:259). All six verify Ed25519/secp256k1 only.
findings.title: Six methods form the signature surface; four sign with a secret key

findings.detail: validation_create (ADMIN-only) generates a secp256k1 validator key pair from a seed and returns the validation private key, the seed, and the 1751 key in the response (ValidationCreate.cpp:54-64). This is the highest-sensitivity output in the RPC surface.
findings.title: validation_create returns a private key in the response

findings.detail: wallet_propose (ADMIN-only) generates an account key pair from a passphrase, seed, or seed_hex, or from a fresh random seed; the default key type is secp256k1 (WalletPropose.cpp:122-136). Passphrase-derived seeds carry a low-entropy warning in the handler itself.
findings.title: wallet_propose derives keys from caller-supplied seed material

findings.detail: The peer-handshake session signature is secp256k1-only: signDigest over a shared value with the node identity key (Handshake.cpp:203), verified with verifyDigest (Handshake.cpp:318). There is no hybrid or PQ peer authentication.
findings.title: Peer-handshake authentication is secp256k1-only

findings.detail: SHA-512-Half is the single hash for ledger and transaction identity: 8 methods return sha512Half-derived hash data and server_definitions is the only handler that computes a hash (ServerInfo.cpp:291). A 256-bit output retains about 128 bits of post-quantum strength against Grover, so no change is required on quantum grounds — but no hash agility exists, so a future hash replacement is a coordinated change.
findings.title: SHA-512-Half is the only hash; no hash agility

findings.detail: The default TLS cipher list is TLSv1.2-only (make_SSLContext.cpp:104) and key exchange is delegated to OpenSSL (SSL_CTX_set_cipher_list, make_SSLContext.cpp:365). No PQ or hybrid key exchange is configured in-tree; negotiated TLS parameters depend on the linked OpenSSL build.
findings.title: TLS is classical-only by default; key exchange is delegated to OpenSSL

findings.detail: doPause and doResume are declared in Handlers.h:110,120 but have no definition and no handler-table entry. They are dead declarations, not methods.
findings.title: doPause/doResume are declared but unregistered and undefined

findings.detail: The gRPC surface is 4 methods (GetLedger, GetLedgerEntry, GetLedgerData, GetLedgerDiff), all read-only ledger queries registered in GRPCServer.cpp:488-549. None signs, verifies, generates keys, or hashes.
findings.title: gRPC surface is ledger reads only; no crypto exposure

findings.detail: 65 of 74 methods perform no cryptographic operation in the handler or its direct helpers. Their only post-quantum exposure is transport (TLS). 8 of the 65 return sha512Half-derived hash data; 1 returns CSPRNG output (random).
findings.title: 65 methods carry no direct crypto exposure
